title: Think2Go: Generative Next POI Recommendation with LLM Reasoning

problem.claim: Next POI recommendation seeks to infer user behavioral preferences from historical check-ins to recommend a personalized next destination.

gap.claim: Existing methods use shallow context and handcrafted feature interactions, while non-reasoning models struggle with sparse and complex mobility patterns and LLMs lack deep understanding of separately trained semantic IDs.

contributions.claim: Think2Go is a generative next POI recommendation framework designed to improve semantic ID comprehension and explore diverse spatial-temporal patterns through test-time computational scaling.
The framework unifies supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement-learning-based reasoning to jointly optimize memorization and adaptive reasoning.
It introduces prompt-uncertainty-based and reward-informed advantage weighting mechanisms for adaptive policy optimization.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe Think2Go as a novel generative next POI recommendation framework.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report extensive experiments on three real-world datasets.
The authors report strong generalization capabilities and improved LLM understanding of semantic IDs.

narrative_sequence.summary: Next POI recommendation mines historical check-ins to suggest a personalized next destination.
Prior methods rely on shallow context, while mobility sparsity and complexity limit reasoning and LLM semantic-ID understanding.
Think2Go combines semantic-ID comprehension improvements with test-time computational scaling.
SFT and RL reasoning are unified, with uncertainty- and reward-informed advantage calibration to support exploration and training stability.
Experiments on three real-world datasets are reported to show strong generalization and improved semantic-ID understanding.

source_observation.claim: The framework combines memorization-oriented supervised fine-tuning with adaptive reinforcement-learning-based reasoning.

interpretation.claim: Recommendation systems may benefit from separating retention of recurring behavior patterns from exploration of less certain preferences.

application.claim: For sequential personalization tasks, consider jointly training behavior memorization and adaptive reasoning components.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this combination helps outside next POI recommendation.

source_observation.claim: Advantage weighting uses estimated epistemic uncertainty and normalized reward magnitude to adjust exploration and update sizes.

interpretation.claim: Instance-aware optimization may reduce entropy collapse and limit overreaction to noisy rewards.

application.claim: In adaptive policy optimization, consider scaling updates according to uncertainty and reward reliability.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify the quantitative effects or conditions under which the calibration is beneficial.

unknowns: The abstract does not provide quantitative experimental results or dataset names.
The abstract does not specify baseline methods, implementation details, or computational costs.
The abstract does not establish independent verification or reproducibility.
